Workflow Automation API + AI Integration Assignment 2

IS 492: Assignment 2 — Automated arXiv Research Alerts with n8n

Build an automated workflow that monitors arXiv for papers in your research area, summarizes the latest result with Groq, and sends a daily email through Gmail.

Background Overview Instructions Additional Features Submission Rubric

Background: n8n and AI-Powered Workflows

n8n is a workflow automation platform that connects data sources, applications, APIs, and AI models. Instead of hiding the process inside one program, n8n represents it as connected nodes, making each step and the data passed between steps visible and testable.

Visual workflow editor
Connected steps and branches make the execution path explicit and inspectable. This helps you understand task decomposition and data flow.
Triggers and inputs
A trigger starts a workflow without requiring a person to run each step manually. In this assignment, the Schedule Trigger starts the workflow at a selected time.
App integrations and data
n8n combines app actions with transformations and custom processing. The output of one node becomes the input of the next.
Execution inspection and debugging
n8n provides tools for inspecting workflow executions and the data moving through individual steps. This helps you locate and diagnose failures.
An automated workflow is not automatically an AI agent

AI-powered workflow: The workflow follows a predefined path, while an AI model performs a particular task within that path.

More agentic system: The model can choose tools or decide some of its next steps based on a goal and the results it observes.

This assignment builds an AI-powered workflow. The connections determine the sequence, and the Groq model is responsible for summarizing the paper abstract.

As you build: Ask what starts each step, what data it receives, what output it produces, and how you can verify that the result is correct.

In this assignment, you will build an automated workflow using n8n that monitors arXiv for new papers in your research area and sends you a daily email with AI-generated summaries. You will connect arXiv’s API, a large language model through Groq, and Gmail into one scheduled pipeline.

By the end, you will have a working system that searches arXiv daily, extracts paper metadata, summarizes the abstract, and delivers a formatted email alert to your inbox.

Learning Objectives
  1. Workflow automation literacy: Design and execute multi-step workflows using triggers, data transformation, and action chaining.
  2. API-based data retrieval: Call the arXiv API, parse XML, and convert the result into structured JSON.
  3. Data transformation and parsing: Select, rename, and clean fields using Set/Edit Fields.
  4. AI integration: Connect a Groq Chat Model to summarize academic text.
  5. Multi-service integration: Combine arXiv, Groq, and Gmail into an end-to-end pipeline.

Instructions

The example below illustrates the core end-to-end workflow.

Example of the complete arXiv to Groq to Gmail workflow

1Create an n8n Account and Workflow

  1. Go to n8n.cloud.
  2. Sign up for the 14-day free trial (no credit card required).
  3. Verify your email and log in.
  4. Create a new blank workflow. Open Personal, then click Create workflow. You may also use the + menu.

2Add Schedule Trigger

  1. Click the + button on the canvas.
  2. Search for Schedule Trigger.
  3. Configure the node:
    • Trigger Interval: Days
    • Days Between Triggers: 1
    • Customization required: Select your own hour, not Midnight. Examples: 9, 10, 18, or 20.
    • Trigger at Minute: 0
  4. Click Execute step to test.

3Call arXiv

  1. Click + after Schedule Trigger.
  2. Search for HTTP Request.
  3. Set Method to GET.
  4. Enter a URL using the structure below. Replace YOUR_TOPIC_HERE with your own research topic.
Base URL Structure
https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?search_query=all:YOUR_TOPIC_HERE&start=0&max_results=1&sortBy=submittedDate&sortOrder=descending
Example URL
https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?search_query=all:human-AI+collaboration&start=0&max_results=1&sortBy=submittedDate&sortOrder=descending
HTTP Request node configured to retrieve an arXiv Atom feed as text
  1. Under Options, click Add option → Response. Set Response Format to Text.
  2. Click Execute step. The output should contain XML data.

4Convert XML to JSON

  1. Click + after HTTP Request.
  2. Search for XML.
  3. Set Mode to XML to JSON.
  4. Set Property Name to data (leave the default value).
  5. Click Execute step. The output should contain a JSON structure.
XML node converting the arXiv response from XML to JSON

5Transform Data and Extract Fields

  1. Click + after the XML node.
  2. Search for Set or Edit Fields.
  3. Select Manual Mapping. Under Fields to Set, add the following fields:
ValueNameExpression
1title{{ $json.feed.entry.title }}
2authors{{ $json.feed.entry.author.map(a => a.name).join(', ') }}
3published{{ $json.feed.entry.published }}
4link{{ $json.feed.entry.id }}
5abstract{{ $json.feed.entry.summary }}
  1. Click Execute step and verify that the output contains clean JSON.
Edit Fields node extracting the five required paper fields

6Add AI Summarization with Groq

n8n’s Groq Chat Model requires an AI Chain node. Complete both parts below.

Part A: Add the Basic LLM Chain

  1. Click + after the Edit Fields node.
  2. Search for LLM Chain or Basic LLM Chain.
  3. Add the node.
  4. Set Source for Prompt (User Message) to Define below.
  5. Enter this prompt:
Summarize this research paper abstract in 3-4 clear sentences for a student: {{ $json.abstract }}
Basic LLM Chain prompt using the paper abstract

Part B: Add and Configure the Groq Chat Model

  1. Below the Basic LLM Chain node, click the + on the required Model connector.
  2. Search for and select Groq Chat Model.
Add a chat model through the required Model connector
  1. Click Connect to Groq.
  2. Paste your Groq API key from console.groq.com into the API Key field.
  3. Click Save.
  4. Confirm that an available model is selected, such as openai/gpt-oss-20b.
  5. Return to the Basic LLM Chain node and click Execute step.
Groq Chat Model configured with an available model and successful output

7Send Email via Gmail

  1. Click + after the Basic LLM Chain node.
  2. Search for Gmail.
  3. Select Send a message.
  4. Click Sign in with Google, choose your account, grant the requested permissions, and return to n8n.
  5. Configure Gmail:
    • Resource: Message
    • Operation: Send
    • To: Your email address
    • Email Type: Text
  6. Use a dynamic subject:
New arXiv Paper: {{ $('Edit Fields').item.json.title }}
  1. Design your own email template. You may adapt this example:
New Research Paper Alert Title: {{ $('Edit Fields').item.json.title }} Authors: {{ $('Edit Fields').item.json.authors }} Published: {{ $('Edit Fields').item.json.published }} Paper Link: {{ $('Edit Fields').item.json.link }} AI Summary: {{ $json.text }} Full Abstract: {{ $('Edit Fields').item.json.abstract }} This is your daily arXiv research update. Thanks, n8n agent demo

If a property name does not resolve, refer to the output of Edit Fields and correct the corresponding expression.

  1. Click Execute step and check your email.
Gmail node configured to send the paper information and AI summary

8Test, Publish, and Export

  1. Click Execute workflow.
  2. Verify that every node on the executed path shows a green checkmark.
  3. Check your email inbox and spam folder.
  4. After successful testing, click Publish to enable scheduled execution.
  5. Export the workflow as a JSON file.

Additional Integration Features

The workflow must include the steps above, plus additional functionality. You may choose from the suggestions below or propose your own.

You must implement at least two additional features beyond the core arXiv → Groq summary → Gmail pipeline. Both features must work and must be demonstrated in your screen recording.
  1. Google Sheets Logging: Save each paper’s metadata to a Google Sheet for long-term tracking.
  2. Conditional Sending: Send an email only if the paper was published within the last 24 hours.
  3. Exploring Multiple Topics: Monitor two or three research topics in one workflow.
    • Duplicate the HTTP Request → XML → Edit Fields sequence for each topic.
    • Merge the results with a Merge node.
    • Format the email to show papers from all topics.
  4. Custom Filtering: Filter papers by a keyword match in the abstract or by specific authors.
  5. Slack or Discord Notification: Send a summary to Slack or Discord in addition to, or instead of, email.
  6. Error Handling: Add an IF node to check whether the API returned a valid result and send a fallback notification if no paper was found.

Submission Instructions

To allow the TAs to grade your n8n workflow configuration, submit the following two files to Canvas.

1. Workflow JSON file
Export the workflow from n8n and name it IS492-A2-YourNetID.json. The JSON contains node configurations but does not include API keys or credentials.
2. Screen recording
Record a successful end-to-end execution. Show green checkmarks, the received email, and a brief verbal explanation of each additional feature and where it appears.

Grading Rubric

1. Workflow Automation Design (20 points)

Score Criteria
20 All nodes are correctly connected and execute without errors. The workflow runs end to end autonomously. Nodes are clearly labeled rather than left with generic default names. For example, use labels such as Schedule Trigger, Fetch arXiv Paper, Parse XML, Summarize with Groq, and Send Gmail. The workflow can be understood without additional explanation.
15 The workflow runs successfully from trigger to email, but node labels are generic or the layout is hard to follow. Minor organizational issues do not affect functionality.
10 One or more nodes are misconfigured or disconnected. The workflow does not execute end to end without manual fixes. For example, the Schedule Trigger is not connected to the HTTP Request, or a node error breaks the chain.
0 The workflow is missing, non-functional, or contains only one or two disconnected nodes.
Common deductions:
  • Leaving the schedule trigger hour at the default (Midnight) instead of customizing it: -2
  • Nodes left with default names and no clear labeling: -3
  • Workflow requires manual node-by-node execution rather than running as a single pipeline: -5

2. API-Based Data Retrieval (20 points)

Score Criteria
20 The query parameters (search_query, max_results, sortBy, and sortOrder) are set correctly. The XML response is received and passed to the next node. The student demonstrates understanding of what the URL parameters do in the recording or workflow notes.
15 The arXiv query is customized for the student’s topic and returns valid results. The XML node converts the response correctly. Minor issues include leaving max_results at 1 or not explaining the parameters.
10 The exact example topic human-AI+collaboration is used without modification, or the HTTP Request node is misconfigured and returns an error or unparseable data.
0 There is no HTTP Request node, or it does not connect to arXiv.
Common errors/deductions:
  • Using the example query topic verbatim without customization: -5
  • Response format not set to "Text" (causing XML parsing to fail silently): -3
  • max_results left at 1 when the workflow claims to handle multiple papers: -2

3. Data Transformation and Parsing (20 points)

Score Criteria
20 All five metadata fields (title, authors, published, link, abstract) are correctly extracted using expressions. The Edit Fields node outputs clean JSON with no leftover raw data. Additional transformations are applied where appropriate, such as date formatting, trimming whitespace, or handling single-author edge cases.
15 All five fields are extracted and the output JSON is correct. No additional cleaning or transformation is applied beyond the minimum.
10 Some fields are missing or use incorrect expressions. For example, authors displays [object Object], or the link points to the wrong field. The JSON is only partially usable.
0 There is no Edit Fields node, or it is present but not configured.
Common deductions:
  • authors field shows raw JSON objects instead of a comma-separated string: -5
  • Missing one of the five required fields: -3 per field
  • Leaving extra/unnecessary fields in the output (not toggling "Keep Only Set"): -2

4. AI Summarization and Email Delivery (20 points)

Score Criteria
20 The Groq LLM Chain uses a thoughtful, customized prompt rather than copying the example verbatim. The summary is coherent and correctly passed to Gmail. The email is well formatted and includes the title, authors, date, link, AI summary, and abstract. The student receives the email successfully, as shown in the recording.
15 The LLM Chain and Gmail nodes work correctly. The prompt is the example prompt or a minor variation. The email contains all required information, but its formatting is minimal or could be improved.
10 Either the LLM Chain or Gmail node fails. Examples include an invalid Groq credential, a prompt that does not reference the abstract, a blank email, or an email missing important fields.
0 There is no LLM or Gmail node, or neither node is functional.
Common deductions:
  • Prompt does not include {{ $json.abstract }} or equivalent (LLM has no input to summarize): -5
  • Email body is missing the AI-generated summary: -3
  • Email subject is hardcoded instead of dynamic: -2
  • Gmail node configured but never tested (no evidence of received email in recording): -5

5. Additional Features and Reflection (20 points)

Score Criteria
20 Two or more additional features are implemented and working. They add meaningful functionality rather than cosmetic changes. In the recording, the student clearly explains each feature and reflects on how the workflow could be extended or applied to their research.
15 Two additional features are implemented and work correctly, but the explanation is brief or surface-level, with limited reflection on broader applicability.
10 Only one additional feature is implemented, or two are attempted but one does not work. The recording includes minimal or no explanation.
0 There are no additional features beyond the base workflow.
Common deductions:
  • Claiming a feature is implemented but it is not visible in the exported JSON or recording: -5 per feature
  • Feature is present but broken (e.g., Google Sheets node added but not authenticated): -3 per feature
  • No verbal explanation of additional features in the recording: -5 per feature
  • Cosmetic-only changes counted as features (e.g., changing the email font): -3 per feature
